subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Reynolds <luke.reynolds@novahealth.com>; Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call so your team and ours have alignment.

Summary (what we heard)
- Current setup: running a mix of self-hosted model endpoints on legacy GPU clusters and a small subset on a 3rd-party LLM API for burst traffic.
- Primary drivers: predictable latency for patient-facing features, cost control, and strict PHI controls (audit logs + KMS).
- Traffic profile: ~500k tokens/day steady, peak burst to ~1.2M tokens. Sequence lengths average 512 tokens for summaries; some shorter prompt-only calls.

Deployment modes we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding and lowest operational lift — good for proof-of-concept and early production with usage-based pricing.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; supports autoscaling policies and isolated capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control for PHI workloads, integrates with customer KMS/HSM and private networking, suitable if Nova Health needs air-gapped or strict regulatory controls.

Initial recommendation (based on discovery)
- Short term: pilot on Redwood Hosted API to validate latency and end-to-end behavior (1-2 weeks), with prefix caching enabled to reduce cost.
- Mid term (if SLA & audit requirements confirmed): Dedicated capacity with reserved pools + KMS integration.
- Private (VPC) only if legal requires customer-managed networking or on-prem compute; we can map out a migration plan if needed.

Open items (please confirm)
1) Do you need customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys (yes/no)?
2) Expected 99th percentile latency SLO you need for patient-facing requests?
3) Any blackout windows or maintenance constraints for migration of current GPUs?

Next steps
- I’ll share a short deployment proposal and a filled security questionnaire (attached) for your security team.
- If you’re comfortable, propose a 30-min technical kickoff next week to review Dedicated sizing & migration plan.

Attachments: Redwood-Deployment-Proposal-RDWD-7683.pdf (proposal), NovaHealth-Security-Questionnaire-filled.xlsx (completed questionnaire)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS/HSM: yes, we need customer-managed keys (we use GCP KMS today).
- Latency SLO: 99th <= 400ms for our interactive features (ideally < 300ms).
- Migration constraints: we have a maintenance freeze 2026-06-10 through 2026-06-14, so any migration work should avoid that window.

Two additional asks: 
1) Can you share high-level cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated for our profile (500k steady / peaks to 1.2M tokens)? A range is fine.
2) What does the migration path look like from our current mix (self-hosted endpoints + third-party API) — do you do API compatibility, or will engineering need to refactor calls?

Happy to do a kickoff next week — Sarah and I are available Tue/Thu mornings PT.

— Luke
Product Lead, AI Platform
Nova Health
luke.reynolds@novahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Reynolds <luke.reynolds@novahealth.com>; Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@novahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration next steps

Thanks Luke — great clarifications. Answers below and attached a short proposal with cost ranges + migration approach.

1) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) in both Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted API can support envelope encryption for keys you hold — for strict PHI controls we typically recommend Dedicated with a KMS integration or Private.

2) Latency: our Dedicated pools with the configuration I’m proposing hit 99th percentile ~200–350ms for 512-token sequences on Ampere-class GPUs with our batching and prefix caching; Hosted API in the same region typically lands 99th ~250–450ms depending on concurrency. We’ll include target latency baselines in the kickoff.

3) Migration path (high level):
- Phase 1: Pilot on Hosted API (validate correctness, prompt tuning, and caching). Minimal code changes — standard REST/SDK calls match common LLM APIs.
- Phase 2: Dedicated sizing & reserved capacity — we’d run a short load test and finalize autoscaling policy (no major code refactor; mostly config and endpoint update).
- Phase 3: Private (if required) — we provide an on-prem package and assist with model weights deployment; this requires coordination with your infra team and a short migration window.

Cost ranges (very rough ballpark for planning)
- Hosted API: $0.XX–$0.YY per 1k tokens (depends on model family and quantization).
- Dedicated: committed monthly, expected 30–50% lower unit cost at your steady state for reserved capacity; detailed numbers in attached proposal.

Action items
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min technical kickoff Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 PT (proposed) — Luke/Sarah to confirm.
- Marissa: share proposal + questionnaire (attached).
- Luke/Sarah: confirm KMS owner contact and whether an SOC2 package review is needed before kickoff.

Attachments: Redwood-Deployment-Proposal-RDWD-7683.pdf, NovaHealth-Security-Questionnaire-filled.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
